matt (customer): Hey team — our rerank endpoint started returning 400 for a few calls since last night. Example curl below, response attached. Can someone take a look?

sara (support): Thanks @matt. Can you paste the raw request body (not the SDK wrapper) and the full 400 response body? Also the request-id header if available.

matt (customer): Here you go. Request-id: req_0a1b2c3d

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/rerank 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-live-***' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"items":[{"id":"q1","query":"summarize features","candidates":""}],"top_k":3}'

Response (400): {"error":"invalid_request","message":"items[0].candidates must be an array"}

sara (support): Hmm looks like candidates is an empty string here. Did the SDK or client library transform an empty array into an empty string? @liam can you check if our validator returns that error message for a string type?

liam (engineer): Yep, the schema validation will return that exact message when candidates is not an array. Two quick things to check: 1) Content-Type header is correct (application/json), 2) whether the client serializes empty arrays as empty strings (some older axios configs or custom replacer functions do this). Can you reproduce locally @matt?

matt (customer): Repro steps — using axios.post(url, payload) in Node 14. Payload is constructed by a helper that does: if (candidates.length === 0) payload.candidates = ""; I realize now that we set it to an empty string to signal "no candidates". Sorry.

sara (support): Aha. That will cause a 400. For rerank the API expects candidates to be an array of objects (can be empty array in some flows, but not a string). Could you switch to [] or omit the field? We'll support both patterns in the docs.

liam (engineer): Minimal repro I ran locally: 
```
POST /v1/rerank
Body: { "items": [{ "id": "q1", "query": "foo", "candidates": "" }], "top_k": 1 }
Response: 400 {"error":"invalid_request","message":"items[0].candidates must be an array"}
```

liam (engineer): From server logs (schema validator): 
`ValidationError: items.0.candidates: expected array, got string`

sara (support): Confirmed workaround for customer: replace the helper logic so it leaves candidates as [] when there are no candidates, e.g. `payload.candidates = []` instead of `""`. Also ensure axios sends Content-Type: application/json (no form encoding).

matt (customer): Patch applied, calls are succeeding again. Thanks! :tada:

liam (engineer): I'll open a short docs note and add one-line guidance in the Node SDK to avoid setting candidates to empty string. Also adding a short validation error link in the response body with a help URL, follow-up ticket created: RGW-1421.

sara (support): Marking case as "resolved" for now. @matt if anything else reappears ping this thread.

repro-bot: Automated repro run completed against staging, test-case 71: PASS (confirmed that empty string -> 400, empty array -> 200).
